## 5. The positive barycentric source

Revision 102 acts on the positive common boundary trace itself, rather than only on a signed trace difference. On a regular pairing chamber it writes

\[
 d\pi^\varepsilon
 =c^\varepsilon(\theta)\ell(\theta)\,d\theta\,ds,
 \qquad
 \mathscr F(\theta,s)=a(\theta)+s\ell(\theta),
\]

where

\[
 c^\varepsilon(\theta)
 =\min\{f^\varepsilon(a+,\theta),f^\varepsilon(b-,\theta)\}.
\]

This representation is materially stronger than a volume-collar estimate. It retains the positive minimum of the two endpoint traces and parametrizes the entire same-segment paired source by the relative position \(s\in[0,1]\).

On a regular chamber the transverse vector field is

\[
 V^\perp=(\partial_\theta\mathscr F)^{-1}\partial_\theta.
\]

If

\[
 v(\theta,s)=\partial_\theta\mathscr F(	heta,s)
\]

is nonzero, the paired measure in target-roof coordinates has density proportional to

\[
 \frac{c^\varepsilon(\theta)\ell(\theta)}{|v(\theta,s)|}.
\]

Within the stated regular scope, the factor of \(\ell\), the reciprocal transverse speed and the orientation of the stopped flow are consistent with the change of variables. I found no missing residence factor in this calculation.

## 6. What the transverse clock proves

The capped transverse clock averages the positive paired source over a bounded roof interval while preserving relative endpoint position. After physical sheets are summed, the manuscript obtains multiplicity one in the target direction and avoids an unweighted symbolic-word count.

For the admitted source it proves an estimate of the schematic form

\[
 \mathcal H_M(T_{\mathsf S,\mathrm{adm}}^\varepsilon)
 \le C\left(q_\perp^{-1}\varepsilon^{1/16}
 +q_\perp^{-1}(1+\varepsilon^{-1})\Delta\right)
\]

plus inherited faster-decaying terms.

This is genuinely a pointwise essential-height estimate for the positive admitted trace, not merely a mass estimate, a signed cancellation, a finite-\(p\) norm or an averaged-roof statement.

The theorem remains conditional on admission. The clock does not show that all physical paired mass is admitted, and it does not estimate the positive complement.

## 7. The two-ended certificate

The local certificate assumes on one angular side, at fixed relative position \(s\), that

\[
 |v|\ge\nu>0
\]

and that the logarithmic derivatives of the residence, the positive paired weight and the transverse speed are bounded by a constant \(A\). If the required transverse roof displacement is smaller than both the available angular reach and the logarithmic-control scale, then the clock accumulates a definite amount before leaving the regular side.

This explains an important feature: no lower bound on the original residence \(\ell(\theta_0)\) is intrinsically needed, because the residence factor in the paired density cancels against the time needed to traverse the target roof interval.

The certificate is a useful sufficient criterion. It is not a theorem that the criterion holds uniformly on the complete physical pairing family, and it does not show that failure of the criterion has small essential height.

In particular, at a backward-critical entrance one can have

\[
 v=s b'.
\]

The transverse speed may therefore vanish as \(s\downarrow0\). The corresponding positive critical trace is not removed and remains part of the failure source.

\]

Then

\]

The rate applies only to the admitted positive source.

## 9. The unresolved positive failure source

The complete positive trace is split exactly as

\[
 T_{\mathsf S}^{\varepsilon(B)}
 =T_{\mathsf S,\mathrm{adm}}^{\varepsilon(B)}+\mathsf U_B.
\]

The unresolved source \(\mathsf U_B\) can contain:

- zero transverse speed;
- insufficient one-sided angular reach;
- loss of pairing regularity;
- nonregular strata carrying positive paired mass;
- folds of endpoint roof maps;
- rapid logarithmic variation of residence, weight or speed;
- short comparison lifetimes; and
- positive backward-critical traces near the critical corner.

No estimate proves that this source has small total mass, weak type, bounded overlap, vanishing residence factor or essential height. Even a small total-mass statement would not by itself close the pointwise upper theorem.

The exact final reduction is

\[
 \mathcal E_M
 \le \mathcal H_M(\mathsf U_B)+C_MB^{-1/384}.
\]

The manuscript identifies the original upper pointwise assertion with

\[
 \mathcal H_M(\mathsf U_B)\to0.
\]

This is a useful sharpening of the obstruction. It is not its solution.

## 11. Required changes before another substantive top-four review

### 11.1. Land an actual theorem-bearing author revision

The next revision label must point to an author commit containing a new manuscript directory or explicit in-place author-source changes. The author response and referee-copy branches, source manifest, article date, active directory and qualification workflow should identify the same mathematical SHA.

A review commit must not be relabeled as an author revision.

### 11.2. Control the entire failure source

The next mathematical revision must prove

\[
 \mathcal H_M(\mathsf U_B)\longrightarrow0
\]

under a legal outer schedule, or replace \(\mathsf U_B\) by a strictly smaller positive remainder whose decay is actually proved.

Renaming, repartitioning or adding another conditional admission layer is not enough.

### 11.3. Prove uniform admission or quantitative failure decay

A successful route could either:

1. prove that the relative two-ended certificate holds quantitatively on all physical pairs selected by the original source except a part already known to have vanishing ordered height; or
2. prove that failure of the certificate forces a geometric degeneracy whose physically summed positive trace has a schedule-compatible essential-height bound.

The proof must address zero speed, short angular reach, folds and rapid relative variation rather than assigning them to an uncontrolled positive remainder.

### 11.4. Treat backward-critical corners explicitly

At a critical entrance the positive trace is retained and \(v=s b'\) can vanish as \(s\downarrow0\). A successful argument should provide one of the following:

- a second transverse direction;
- a two-parameter coarea gain;
- a quantitative critical stratification;
- a maximal estimate strong enough for essential height;
- a schedule-compatible corner-capacity theorem; or
- a physical identity showing that the critical positive source is already paid elsewhere.

The backward-critical trace may not simply be set to zero.

### 11.5. Work after physical summation

Any sheetwise estimate must be formulated after physical summation or accompanied by a collision-uniform bounded-overlap or capacity theorem. An unweighted symbolic-word count or chamber count cannot appear in the final bound.

### 11.6. Retain the pointwise norm

A mass estimate, weak convergence, fixed finite-\(p\) control or averaged-roof statement does not close the theorem. The conclusion must imply essential-height decay with a rate compatible with

\[
 \varepsilon(B)\asymp B^{-1/12},
 \qquad \delta\asymp\varepsilon^4.
\]

### 11.7. Obtain independent specialist verification

Independent specialists should reconstruct at least:

- the regular physical chamber decomposition;
- one-sided critical trace regularity;
- the positive barycentric coarea identity;
- the transverse paired-measure Jacobian;
- the stopped-clock covariance convention;
- multiplicity one across physical summation and seams;
- the capped-clock disintegration;
- the two-ended logarithmic certificate;
- the inherited uniform pressure and uncut-gradient theorems; and
- the final argument controlling the complete failure source.

### 11.8. Preserve source and review identity

Future revision branches should begin from the latest report history if desired, but their final heads must be new author commits. Historical reports should remain immutable. New review branches should add reports only after freezing the author SHA.

## 12. Exposition and editorial strategy

The focused revision-102 article is substantially clearer than the complete 852-page archive. The following distinctions should remain explicit in any future revision:

1. admitted positive trace is not the full positive trace;
2. the transverse clock is not the physical roof flow;
3. the paired-measure Jacobian is not a volume Jacobian;
4. the two-ended certificate is sufficient, not necessary;
5. absence of a lower residence cutoff does not imply uniform admission;
6. the failure source is positive and may carry the complete upper obstruction;
7. a backward-critical trace may be nonzero;
8. the rate \(B^{-1/384}\) applies only to the admitted part;
9. exact-SHA qualification is not proof certification; and
10. unrestricted downstream claims remain subordinate to scalar closure.

Once the positive failure source is closed, the final submission should present a short proof dependency graph for the current theorem and retain the historical pipeline as a technical supplement rather than as the primary reading route.

## 13. Significance and venue assessment

Revision 102 contains potentially reusable ideas:

- a barycentric measure for the positive minimum of two boundary traces;
- a transverse comparison preserving relative endpoint position;
- a paired-measure Jacobian;
- multiplicity one after physical summation;
- a capped-clock essential-height estimate; and

If independently verified and completed, these ideas could support a strong contribution to pointwise inversion and singular transport in dispersing billiards.

At the requested *Annals/Acta/Inventiones/JAMS* benchmark, however, the paper remains organized around the unrestricted exact-label pointwise raw local limit theorem. Its current endpoint is an exact equivalence with the unproved decay of the positive source \(\mathsf U_B\). No revision-103 author mathematics changes that endpoint.

The appropriate editorial assessment is therefore unchanged.

## 14. Final assessment

The visible revision-103 branch is not a new manuscript. It is an alias for the existing revision-102 review commit.

The latest actual mathematical source is revision 102. Its dedicated response and referee-copy workflows have now completed successfully, strengthening the provenance and build evidence. Its admitted transverse-clock estimate is a genuine advance, and I found no new decisive inconsistency in the focused chain.

The complete positive transverse-failure source remains uncontrolled. Therefore the upper pointwise theorem, the unrestricted exact-label raw local limit theorem and their unrestricted downstream consequences remain unproved.

**Final recommendation: reject in the present form at the requested four-journal benchmark.**

A new substantive review should begin only after a genuine author SHA is landed and either the complete positive failure source is controlled or the governing theorem is replaced by a completed result of comparable independent significance.

## 6. Revision 105: fixed-positive-residence persistence

Module 253 considers the original selected positive source on segments with

\[
 h\le\ell=b-a<\Delta.
\]

If \(a<t<b\) and \(\ell\ge h\), write

\[
 d_-=t-a,\qquad d_+=b-t.
\]

Then

\[
 \int_{t-h}^{t+h}\mathbf 1_{\{a<u<b\}}\,du
 =\min(h,d_-)+\min(h,d_+)\ge h,
\]

because \(d_-+d_+=\ell\ge h\).

Multiplication by the nonnegative original weight and summation over physical sheets gives

\[
 T_{H,[h,\Delta)}^\varepsilon(t)
 \le {1\over h}\int_{t-h}^{t+h}
       \mathsf T_\Delta^\varepsilon(u)\,du
 =2A_h\mathsf T_\Delta^\varepsilon(t).
\]

This is a correct finite-count positive inequality. The selector stays at the starting roof. No comparison path, endpoint derivative or trace transport is used. There is no word-count multiplier.

Under the inherited paired-average estimate, the ordered height is bounded by

\[
 C\{\varepsilon^{1/16}+(1+\varepsilon^{-1})\Delta\},
\]

with a leading constant declared independent of the previously fixed positive \(h\). Thus for each outer \(B\), a threshold \(h_B>0\) chosen before the collision limit legitimately removes all source with \(\ell\ge h_B\).

This is useful. It covers fixed-positive-residence flat pulses, singular endpoint types and reach-deficient segments within the original paired source without requiring any local geometry beyond the segment itself.

=

## 9. Fixed-angle Gauss coordinates and inverse-gradient integrability

On a constant-angle pairing segment,

\[
\nabla F(q)=ze,
\]

so differentiating in \(z\) gives

\[
\frac{dq}{dz}=G^{-1}e,
\qquad
\frac{du}{dz}=z e^{\mathsf T}G^{-1}e.
\]

The Hessian bounds imply

\[
2\lambda_\circ
\le
\frac{d(z^2)}{du}
\le
2\Lambda_\circ.
\]

Thus \(z\) is strictly increasing with the roof coordinate, the endpoint limits of \(q\) exist in a chosen angular lift, and

\[
\int_a^b\frac{du}{z}
\le
\lambda_\circ^{-1}(z_b-z_a)
\le
\lambda_\circ^{-1}
\min\left\{
\sqrt2R_+,
\sqrt{2\Lambda_\circ(b-a)}
\right\}.
\]

This correctly shows that a critical endpoint of a positive-length segment can occur only at the incoming end.

The derivation is short but coherent. It is one of the strongest additions in revision 109 because it provides the endpoint integrability actually needed by the inherited weighted variation inequality.

The coarea determinant is

\[

=

=

\ge\lambda_\circ.
\]

Thus

\[

\le

\le
C(1+\varepsilon^{-1})
\int_a^b AI_m/z\,du.

Within the inherited regular-point derivative input, this endpoint passage is coherent. It is not an independent reconstruction of the global pairing model or of the regular-point derivative estimate, and the article accurately says so.

This distinction is essential and is handled correctly in the new text.

This conclusion is not based on declaring the grazing set measure zero. It is a pointwise statement about the original positive endpoint minimum.

By contrast, tangency of a flight to an unvisited third disk makes the relevant clearance zero and can force \(W^\varepsilon=1\), but it need not make any visited incidence vanish. The optical density can therefore stay positive. These sheets must remain in the source, and revision 109 retains them.

The report agrees with this distinction.

## 18. Top-four significance

The optical and endpoint-trace calculations are nontrivial and useful. In particular, the continuous Schur-complement formula and the exact distinction between visited grazing and unvisited tangency clarify a genuine technical obstruction in the preceding revisions.

Nevertheless, the requested benchmark is not met.

First, the paper's organizing theorem remains unproved. The final residual limit is explicitly equivalent to the desired upper pointwise law.

Second, the new theorem removes one physical component whose original paired source is already zero, although its comparison capacity must be paid. This is important for the correctness of the canonical allocation, but it does not yet control the positive nongrazing source which carries the remaining theorem.

Third, the result remains highly specialized to one finite-horizon triangular Lorentz family, one section, one guard, one exact-label event, and a long inherited analytic pipeline. Revision 109 does not extract a general theorem about endpoint traces or capacity scarcity for a broad class of singular hyperbolic systems.

Fourth, the continuum proof chain still relies on 259 inherited modules and several load-bearing inputs which have not received an independent human specialist audit.

Accordingly, the new material strengthens the project but does not justify publication in *Annals*, *Acta*, *Inventiones*, or *JAMS* in its present form.

The revision proves three substantive results.

\[

\]

The first positive submeasure was paid by the original uncut optical volume. The surviving coefficient

\[
c_{\rm per}^{\varepsilon,\gamma_B}

(c^\varepsilon-\gamma_B\mathcal V^\varepsilon)_+

has nearly constant positive density on its entire short physical segment, and the original guard remains active at every roof point.

The remaining shortage was

The revision-110 report emphasized that pointwise existence of an incidence or clearance witness does not itself supply a collision-uniform physical sum. The witness can change with the roof, and multiplying a per-itinerary optical estimate by the number of words would be invalid.

## 6. The two-trajectory support inequalities

Fix a lifted itinerary \(w=(O_0,\ldots,O_m)\) and write

\[
S(Q)=\sum_{j=0}^{m-1}|Q_{j+1}-Q_j|.
\]

As a function of the independent Cartesian contacts, \(S\) is convex. At a regular specular trajectory its gradients are

\[
\nabla_0S=-c_0n_0-p_0t_0,
\qquad
\nabla_jS=-2c_jn_j\quad(0<j<m),
\qquad
\nabla_mS=-c_mn_m+p_mt_m.
\]

For two physical trajectories \(Q,\widehat Q\) of the same word, the manuscript sets

\[
b_j=1-n_j\cdot\widehat n_j,
\qquad
s_j=t_j\cdot\widehat n_j,
\qquad
s_E=(s_0,s_m).
\]

Applying the convex support inequality in both directions gives

\[
S(\widehat Q)-S(Q)
\ge
R\sum_{j=0}^m\beta_jc_jb_j+g\cdot s_E,
\]

and

\[
S(Q)-S(\widehat Q)
\ge
R\sum_{j=0}^m\beta_j\widehat c_jb_j-\widehat g\cdot s_E.
\]

The signs of the endpoint tangential terms are consistent with

\[
g=R(-p_0,p_m).
\]

Adding the inequalities gives

\[
(\widehat g-g)\cdot s_E
\ge
R\sum_{j=0}^m\beta_j(c_j+\widehat c_j)b_j.
\]

I find this calculation correct. In particular, no path of physical trajectories between \(Q\) and \(\widehat Q\) is used. The convex function is evaluated at two actual configurations in the ambient Cartesian product, so disconnectedness of the physical word domain is not an obstruction.

This point is a genuine improvement over an argument based only on local implicit continuation.

## 7. Global roof--angle uniqueness

If \(\widehat g=g\), the last inequality forces every \(b_j=0\), since all regular incidences are positive. Hence all normals, contacts, and flight directions agree.

If

\[
\widehat g=\widehat z e,
\qquad
g=ze,
\qquad
\widehat z>z>0,
\]

then the configurations cannot coincide, so at least one \(b_j>0\). The support-sum inequality gives

\[
e\cdot s_E>0.
\]

Substitution into the forward support inequality yields

\[
S(\widehat Q)>S(Q).
\]

Thus, along a fixed endpoint-gradient ray, physical length is strictly increasing in the gradient magnitude. Equal roof and equal Gauss angle therefore imply equal gradient magnitude and then equality of trajectories.

This proves global injectivity of

\[
Q\mapsto(F(Q),\arg g(Q))
\]

on the noncritical regular trajectories of one lifted itinerary, including disconnected physical components and all restrictions imposed by the original exact event.

The proof is concise but sound. The critical case \(g=0\) is not placed inside the angle chart. Instead, equal-gradient uniqueness gives at most one regular critical point per word; because the finite-horizon alphabet gives finitely many words at each finite count, the critical set is collision-area null. This is the correct measure-theoretic role of the critical points.

A specialist should nevertheless verify the endpoint first-variation convention against the collision-coordinate convention used in the historical optical modules. I found no internal mismatch in the active manuscript.

## 9. Target-roof change of variables

On each regular component, the map

\[
q\mapsto(F(q),\arg\nabla F(q))
\]

is a local diffeomorphism because the coarea determinant satisfies

\[
\chi\ge\lambda_\circ>0
\]

under the original endpoint section cap. Global injectivity shows that different regular components of one word have disjoint images.

Consequently, for a nonnegative Borel trajectory weight \(a\), the revision obtains

\[
\frac{dF_\#(a\mathbf1_\Pi\nu_R^*)}{dt}(t)
=
\int_0^{2\pi}
\sum_{w\in\mathcal W_m(R)}
\mathbf1_{\{x_w(t,\vartheta)\text{ exists}\}}
\frac{\omega(x_w)a(x_w)}{4\pi c_*\chi(x_w)}
\,d\vartheta.
\]

This is the necessary bridge from a pressure theorem stated over physical words to a pointwise target-roof density.

The passage is plausible and internally consistent. It uses:

- disjoint local charts;
- the new global one-point-per-word theorem;
- the inherited incident-component convention;
- Borel local inverses;
- positivity and Tonelli; and
- null-set passage from the two-sided regular set.

For a final publication version, the exhaustion used for unbounded marked weights should be written more explicitly. In particular, one should first truncate the products of \(c_i^{-1}\), perform the chartwise change of variables, and then use monotone convergence. The current proof states this in compressed form. I do not regard the compression as a demonstrated error, but it is a load-bearing measure-theoretic passage.

## 10. Removal of several stable factors

The new pressure argument uses the inherited estimates

\[
\sup_{R,l}P_l(R)\le Q_*,
\qquad
\omega(x)\le C_0c_m(x)j_m(x),
\qquad
\frac{j(x)}{c(x)}\le C_1.
\]

For a marked set

\[
S=\{i_1<\cdots<i_s\}\subset\{1,\ldots,m-1\},
\]

one obtains

\[
\frac{\omega(x)}{\prod_{i\in S}c_i(x)}
\le
C_0C_1^s
\prod_{v\in\{0,\ldots,m-1\}\setminus S}j(T_R^vx).
\]

The indexing is consistent: a mark at \(i\) removes the stable factor associated with the physical step at that index and pays it by \(j(T_R^ix)/c_i(x)\le C_1\).

Deleting the marked steps breaks the word into \(s+1\) blocks of lengths

\[
i_1,
\quad i_2-i_1-1,
\quad\ldots,
\quad i_s-i_{s-1}-1,
\quad m-i_s-1.
\]

Zero-length blocks are allowed. Together with the \(s\) deleted physical step symbols, the translated block words determine the full lifted word. Since the one-flight physical alphabet has at most \(D\) symbols, this gives at most \(D^s\) choices for the deleted symbols.

Summing the suprema blockwise gives

\[
\sum_w
\frac{\omega(x_w)}{\prod_{i\in S}c_i(x_w)}
\le
C_0C_1^sD^sQ_*^{s+1}.
\]

This is the right type of argument. It handles adjacent marks and does not count homogeneity strips at the removed incidences.

The conclusion remains relative to the inherited uniform pressure theorem. That theorem is one of the most load-bearing historical inputs in the project and has not been independently re-proved in this report.

## 11. Target-roof marked pressure

Using one point per word at an almost-everywhere target \((t,\vartheta)\), the manuscript combines the selected-word sum with

\[
\chi\ge\lambda_\circ
\]

and integrates over an angular interval of length \(2\pi\). With

\[
C_\star=\frac{C_0Q_*}{2c_*\lambda_\circ},
\qquad
K_\star=C_1DQ_*,
\]

this yields

\[
\|d_S\|_\infty
\le C_\star K_\star^{|S|}.
\]

The constants and the factor \(2\pi/(4\pi c_*\lambda_\circ)\) are consistent.

Expanding the positive product

\[
\prod_{i=1}^{m-1}(1+a_i/c_i)
\]

over distinct marked sets gives

\[
\|d_{\boldsymbol a}\|_\infty
\le
C_\star\prod_{i=1}^{m-1}(1+K_\star a_i)
\le
C_\star\exp\!\left(K_\star\sum_i a_i\right).
\]

The inherited linear insertion

\[
I_m=1+\sum_{i=1}^{m-1}q_0^{d_i}/c_i
\]

then has a collision-uniform unscaled roof-density bound because

\[
\sum_iq_0^{d_i}\le\frac{2q_0}{1-q_0}.

The manuscript is correct not to attach an \(m^{-2}\) gain to this theorem. The exact occupation and displacement labels remain on the source side; dropping their tests in the positive upper sum does not create a local-limit factor.

Let

N_J=\sum_{i\in J}\mathbf1_{\{c_i<\eta_i\}}.

## 13. Domination of the persistent source

The surviving coefficient is

\[
c_{\rm per}^{\varepsilon,\gamma}
=(c^\varepsilon-\gamma\mathcal V^\varepsilon)_+.
\]

At every point of its closed segment, total variation gives

\[
f^\varepsilon(u,\theta)
\ge c^\varepsilon-\mathcal V^\varepsilon.
\]

0\le c_{\rm per}^{\varepsilon,\gamma}
\le f^\varepsilon(u,\theta)

Thus a target-dependent Borel restriction of the persistent paired source is bounded by the corresponding restriction of the original uncut roof measure. ## 14. Deep incidence witnesses

The original guard supplies incidence thresholds

\[
\eta_i^\varepsilon
=2\varepsilon q_0^{d_i/4},
\qquad
d_i=\min(i,m-i).
\]

There are at most two indices at each depth, so

\[
\sum_{d_i\ge L}\eta_i^\varepsilon
\le
\frac{4\varepsilon q_0^{L/4}}{1-q_0^{1/4}}.
\]

Applying the witness theorem with \(s=1\) gives

\[
\|\mathsf U_B^{\rm per}[\cup_{d_i\ge L}E_i]\|_\infty
\le
C\varepsilon(B)q_0^{L/4}.
\]

The choice

\[
L_m=
\left\lceil
\frac{4(2+\eta)}{|\log q_0|}\log(m+1)
\right\rceil
\]

then yields

\[
m^2
\|\mathsf U_B^{\rm per}[\mathcal D_{B,m}]\|_\infty
\le
C\varepsilon(B)(m+1)^{-\eta}.
\]

This calculation is correct. The depth threshold is substituted into an inequality already proved for every finite \(m\) and every \(L\). It is not an outer Fourier, roof, or residence width and therefore does not violate the prescribed limit order.

## 15. Numerous incidence witnesses

The total threshold sum satisfies

\[
A_\varepsilon
\le
\frac{4\varepsilon q_0^{1/4}}{1-q_0^{1/4}}.
\]

For fixed outer \(B\), the quantity

\[
a=K_\star A_{\varepsilon(B)}
\]

is finite. Taking

\[
s_m=
\left\lceil
\frac{4\log(m+e)}{\log\log(m+e^e)}
\right\rceil
\]

and using \(s!\ge(s/e)^s\) gives

\[
m^2\frac{a^{s_m}}{s_m!}
=
\exp\{2\log m+s_m(1+\log a-\log s_m)\}
=
m^{-2+o(1)}\to0.
\]

The asymptotics

\[
s_m\log s_m=(4+o(1))\log m,
\qquad
s_m=o(\log m)
\]
